claims.explanation: Zolantidine is annotated as a histamine H2 receptor antagonist, but the selective killing pattern across these lines does not track with H2 receptor biology; instead, sensitivity is strongly enriched in lines with RAS/PI3K pathway activation (KRAS, PIK3CA, PTEN loss, NF1 loss) and in neural-crest-derived lineages (melanoma, neuroblastoma, glioma), suggesting the drug's selectivity is driven by dependence on a growth-factor/PI3K-MAPK signaling axis rather than histamine receptors. The virtual-cell response (up PRKCH/PLCB3, down PSMB8/CHAC1) and similarity to receptor antagonists/ion-channel blockers are consistent with a non-canonical off-target effect on calcium/lipid signaling that preferentially kills RAS/PI3K-driven tumors.

features.basis: KRAS-mutant lines (KPNSI9S, NCIH1792, GP2D, SNU410, PATU8988T) are enriched among sensitive lines
PTEN loss co-occurs in sensitive lines (KALS1, UACC62, GP2D, HEC265, ZR751)
PIK3CA-mutant lines (HGC27, GP2D, KYSE510, KYSE70) appear among sensitive lines
NF1 loss in sensitive lines (KALS1, LOXIMVI, GP2D, BICR6) suggests MAPK dependence
BRAF-mutant melanoma/endometrial lines (LOXIMVI, UACC62, HEC265) are sensitive
TP53 mutation is nearly universal and does not distinguish sensitive from resistant lines
SMARCA4-mutant lines (COV434, OV7) appear in sensitive set
ARID1A loss in several sensitive lines (LOXIMVI, GP2D, HEC265, KYSE70)
STK11-mutant lines (NCIH1623, SNU840, TE4) are among least affected
SF3B1-mutant lines (CAL12T, LS1034, UO31, TE4) are among least affected
CDKN2A loss appears in resistant lines (CAL12T, YD10B, 8305C, SNU899)
HRAS-mutant bladder lines (T24, SNU899) are among least affected
